seo.title: HubGet vs UniGetUI – comparison
seo.description: HubGet vs UniGetUI: an App Store-style app store, or a mature package manager for many package managers at once? A fair feature comparison.
seo.ogDescription: An App Store-style app store, or a mature package manager? A feature comparison of HubGet and UniGetUI.

texty.t5: UniGetUI is a mature and popular package manager with a graphical interface – and in many ways it’s ahead of HubGet today. HubGet takes a different path: instead of a package list, it’s an app store where you discover, compare and install apps like in the App Store.
texty.t13: Today · Collections · Charts · App of the Day
texty.t24: Packages from many managers in one list
texty.t35: What each tool can do. Where UniGetUI is ahead, we say so.
texty.t40: {info}A desktop app store for Windows 10 and 11
texty.t43: {yes}WinGet, Chocolatey, Scoop and, since version 0.1.13, developer managers too: npm, Bun, pip, Cargo, vcpkg, .NET Tool, PowerShell 7 and 5
texty.t44: {yes}WinGet, Scoop, Chocolatey, PowerShell 5 and 7, npm, Bun, pip, Cargo, .NET Tool and vcpkg
texty.t46: {yes}A Today home page with App of the Day, collections by focus, charts and categories
texty.t47: {partly}Package search across managers with detailed information
texty.t49: {yes}An app from several managers has a single card with every source – you choose where to install from
texty.t52: {yes}A banner in the icon’s colors, a screenshot gallery, SHA-256, dependencies and terminal commands
texty.t53: {yes}Detailed package information, including screenshots from a community database
texty.t55: {yes}Average star rating, rating breakdown and the most helpful reviews – add your own after signing in with GitHub
texty.t58: {yes}Right in the app, in bulk too – for every supported manager
texty.t59: {yes}For every supported manager, in bulk too
texty.t61: {yes}When WinGet reports a broken download link, HubGet automatically tries Chocolatey and then Scoop
texty.t62: {no}Doesn’t try another source on its own when an install fails
texty.t64: {yes}Finds leftovers in AppData, Program Files, the Start menu and the registry and offers to delete them. With install tracking, it knows everything the installer created
texty.t65: {no}Uninstalls through the package manager without looking for leftovers
texty.t67: {yes}Scheduled checks and installs (at an interval, daily or on selected days at a set time), notifications, a minimum age for updates, a warning when the installer host changes and exceptions for battery, battery saver and metered connections
texty.t70: {yes}Regular user mode shows desktop apps only; Developer mode adds libraries and tools
texty.t71: {info}One interface for every kind of package
texty.t73: {yes}A tray icon – installs finish even after you close the window
texty.t76: {yes}Everything that starts when you sign in to Windows, in one place – turn items on or off with one click and see their impact on startup
texty.t79: {yes}Package bundles with import and export (.ubundle, PowerShell script, WinGet export)
texty.t80: {yes}Export and import of package lists, plus backups to a GitHub Gist
texty.t89: Each one fits a different job.
texty.t90: {ikona} HubGet is a good fit if you…

texty.t92: want one card per app, no matter how many managers offer it
texty.t93: want a simple interface without libraries and developer tools
texty.t94: want HubGet to try another source automatically when a WinGet link is broken
texty.t95: UniGetUI is a good fit if you…
texty.t96: want one list of packages from every manager instead of an app store

texty.t100: Is HubGet an alternative to UniGetUI?
texty.t101: For regular Windows users, yes. UniGetUI is a powerful tool for managing packages from many managers. HubGet focuses on making app installs as pleasant as in the app store on your phone – with recommendations, collections, one card per app and a simple mode without developer tools.
texty.t103: UniGetUI can back up your package list to a GitHub Gist. Both now offer the same package managers and automatic updates – since version 0.1.13, HubGet manages npm, Bun, pip, Cargo, vcpkg, .NET Tool and PowerShell in addition to WinGet, Chocolatey and Scoop, and schedules updates at a set time, with a minimum age and battery exceptions.
texty.t104: Can I use HubGet and UniGetUI side by side?
texty.t105: Yes. Both tools work with the same package managers. Apps installed through UniGetUI show up in HubGet’s installed apps overview, and vice versa.
texty.t107: Yes. Both HubGet and UniGetUI are open source under the MIT license and free.
texty.t109: Free, open source and ad-free. The installer is about 6 MB and doesn’t need admin rights.
